hello: Hey! The bowl's empty right now, which never happens. I've got a spare board if you want it.
first: First time in a bowl? Easy: you drop in off the coping, and {k:W} on the way down gives you speed. That's pumping.
Hit the wall fast and you fly. In the air: {k:J} kickflip, {k:K} grab, {k:A} {k:D} spin a 180. Just land with the board along the wall.
Next to the coping, or over the bar, {k:L} is a grind. A few tricks in a row without falling is a combo, and it multiplies. You've got one minute.
go: Take the red board. It's kind to people who respect it.
after: {score}! Not bad at all. Your best: {best}. Another one?
again: {score}. The bowl beats everyone at first. Your best is still {best}.
best: {score}?! New best! I'm sending this to the skate park group.
quit: The bowl isn't going anywhere. I'm here till they turn the lights off.
later: Cool. I'm here till they turn the lights off.

hello: Hi, welcome aboard Arkia-ish! I'm Gal, your flight attendant today. Sit anywhere you like, we're running a little late.
where: To Eilat! That was the plan, anyway. The captain said he knew a shortcut through Rishon's dunes, and here we are.
Honestly? Sea view, quiet, nobody kicking your seat. I'm in no hurry.
drink: Sure! Water, orange juice, or tea I made three hours ago. I'd go with the water.
And since you're a special passenger, have a pretzel too. Don't tell the others, there are none left.
safety: The exits are here, here, and... actually just here. One door is open, and the stairs are waiting outside.
In case of a landing on sand? We already landed on sand. So you're covered.
bye: Thanks for flying with us! Don't forget your things in the overhead bin, and come back any time.

m18_mayor.title: The mayor arrives after the encore
m18_mayor.cheer: The mayor on drums. Left, right, and left again.

obj.huddle: Hear out the mayor with the band
obj.name: Pick a name for the event with Dekel
obj.lesson: Drum with Malul so Raz can find the beat
obj.plan: Hear what Raz has planned for tomorrow

c.saturday: "Saturday night at the City Hall square"

offer: The stage is almost empty. A man in a navy jacket runs across the square, phone to his ear, and stops right in front of Malul's drums.
Wait, wait, don't pack up! ...Yes, I'm on the line. Tell them I'm already there. ...No, not there. Here.
Raz, the mayor. Nice to meet you. Tonight I did a bar mitzvah, a community garden opening and the seniors' backgammon tournament. I lost. And now I'm here, and I missed the show of the year.
I know. I saw the page. Half the city posted a photo of whoever sat next to them. First time that page has posted anything that isn't about parking.
So I have an idea. Or a request. Or an idea that is really a request. Call the guys over?
huddle: Bro, the mayor? Really? I thought he was from the generator's insurance.

I know them too. Listen: what happened here tonight, religious, secular, grandmothers, skaters, all on the same square... I want it every month. A city event. A stage, chairs, real power. Not one generator and a prayer.
Every month? Like a steady workout. It hurts at first, then you can't do without it.
Bro, I'm filming this! ...No. I'm not filming. I swore. Just listening.
One thing. An event needs a name. All I've got are names like "Intergenerational Community Gathering, courtesy of the Culture Department". Save me.
name: dekel
A name matters. It's what people say when they invite someone else to come.
dekel
So what do you say?
rChair: "Bring a chair, bring someone." ...I feel like we stole that from a grandmother.
It's Savta Rachel's. She'll be happy. She'll say she isn't, but she will.
rSpirits: Four Spirits every month! Bro, I need a new drum skin.
The Culture Department will buy it. Write that down. ...Nobody's writing? Fine, I'll write it.
rSaturday: Saturday night. We start after Havdalah, so everyone can come. Those waiting for three stars, and those waiting for a parking spot.
Wow. That's exactly what my dad would say. Just with more verses.
lesson: And now a personal request. I always wanted to drum. When I was twelve my mother said: "Just not in the house." So here I am. Not in the house.
Okay, Mr Mayor. I play, you watch my hands, and our friend here holds the beat so we don't get lost. One, two, three, four.
lessonDone: Raz drums on a plastic chair. Not well, but with the joy of a man who waited forty years for it. His phone rings in the middle, and he doesn't answer. First time tonight.
Wallah, you've got a hand. The left one. The right one is still deciding.
Nobody tells me that in meetings.
plan: Right. Tomorrow morning I do a round: the Heichal, the Teder and the Great Synagogue. A stage, the youth and chairs. If everyone says yes, we have an event.
One small problem. My driver is at his grandson's bris. And I don't drive. Really don't. The city asked nicely.
You. We meet at the City Hall square. I'll bring coffee. ...I'll bring two, one always spills.
Drive slowly. He sounds like a man who spills coffee from a cup with a lid.

m18_mayor.page: 📱 Rishon Unfiltered: did anyone see the mayor drumming on a chair at the City Hall square at midnight? (1,204 likes. Three comments about parking, out of habit.)

m20_certificate.title: A certificate of appreciation

obj.gather: Hear Raz's speech at the City Hall square
obj.who: Decide who Raz gives the certificate to
obj.photo: Stand with everyone for the photo

c.malul: "To Malul. He always counts to four first"
c.savta: "To Savta Rachel. She started the page"

offer: The City Hall square, six in the evening. Someone rolled out a red carpet that is too short and ends halfway up the steps.
You came! And in shirts! ...Adir, that's a tank top.
Approved. Come, I don't start without everyone. And without Savta Rachel I don't start at all.
speechChair: Friends, neighbours, Savta Rachel. I'll be brief. ...I'm never brief, but I'll try.
Not long ago the city's page was a place where everyone shouted. Then four guys with a drum, a ukulele, keys and... Adir, what do you play?
Guitar. Weights too, but not at shows.
Four guys, and everyone who helped them, sat the whole city down on one square. So from next month it's official: "Bring a chair, bring someone", once a month, at the City Hall square.
That's mine, you know. The name.
I know, Savta Rachel. That's why it's good. And now, a certificate of appreciation. Only one, because the city printer ran out of gold.
speechSpirits: Friends, neighbours, Savta Rachel. I'll be brief. ...I'm never brief, but I'll try.
Not long ago the city's page was a place where everyone shouted. Then four guys with a drum, a ukulele, keys and... Adir, what do you play?
Guitar. Weights too, but not at shows.
Four guys, and everyone who helped them, sat the whole city down on one square. So from next month it's official: "Four Spirits, every month", at the City Hall square. With a new drum skin.
A budget for the drum! Bro, this is the most moving moment of my life.
And now, a certificate of appreciation. Only one, because the city printer ran out of gold.
speechSaturday: Friends, neighbours, Savta Rachel. I'll be brief. ...I'm never brief, but I'll try.
Not long ago the city's page was a place where everyone shouted. Then four guys with a drum, a ukulele, keys and... Adir, what do you play?
Guitar. Weights too, but not at shows.

Four guys, and everyone who helped them, sat the whole city down on one square. So from next month it's official: "Saturday night at the City Hall square". A quarter of an hour after Shabbat ends, not a minute before.
He remembered. You see, Avi? He remembered.
And now, a certificate of appreciation. Only one, because the city printer ran out of gold.
who: So who do I give it to? I'd give it to everyone, but it's one frame.
rMalul: Me? Bro... one, two, three... I've got no four. First time I've got no four.
Film this! ...No. Don't film. Just watch.
rSavta: I opened a page for a cat. Not for certificates.
...But I'll hang it on the fridge. Next to the magnet with the password.
rAll: To everyone? ...Fine. Then I write here: "To everyone who brought a chair, and someone". Does that include me? I brought coffee.
outro: Applause. Shimon raises an orange over his head like a trophy. Raz's phone rings, and he switches it off. Everyone sees.
This is for you. Not for a photo. ...Fine, also for a photo. Squeeze in.
I'm filming! This time from start to finish. Nothing cut.
On the page, the week's favourite photo: the whole crew at the City Hall square, the mayor in the middle with his eyes closed. Nobody writes about parking.

sm01_cape.title: The Cape in the Crate

obj.savta: Talk to Savta Rachel by the crate
obj.secret: Decide with Moshiko who knows the new identity
obj.suit: Back to Moshiko to suit up (then V switches to Super Malul)

c.all: "We tell everyone. The city needs a hero"

offer: City Hall plaza. Moshiko rolls a crate marked "Weddings, fragile, no Carlebach".
Bro. I found something I left years ago for a cousin's wedding. ...Don't ask who the cousin was.
It's a suit. Blue, a star, red boots. Malul, it's for you. Savta Rachel already knows, ask her.
savta: Finally. How long have I waited for someone to climb a roof in a cape.
For years I've watched you help old ladies cross. No suit. With a suit at least they'll notice.
Just remember: a hero doesn't look away. Even from the car parked at the corner.
secret: I'm not sure I'm a hero. I'm a drummer.
Same in theatre. Who gets to know it's you?
rAll: He knew before you. Don't worry.
rSecret: A secret. But I need a name.
"Super Malul". It's already on the crate, in marker.
rSavta: Fine. I'll keep the secret. Mostly from Orit.
suit: Go on, suit up. ...Not here. Behind the stand.
Malul steps out in blue, red and a star. A few passers-by stop. One honks.
You can now press V any time: it switches between regular Malul and Super Malul.

sm01_cape.page: 📱 Rishon Without a Filter: someone in blue with a star crossed City Hall plaza and made a bin disappear. (1,877 likes. One comment: "who is that?". Another: "save him a chair".)

sm02_patrol.title: First Patrol

obj.cross: Help Pnina cross by the Great Synagogue
obj.sidekick: Decide what to do about Dudi, who wants to join

c.yes: "Fine, be the sidekick. But I decide"

offer: By the Teder. A fourteen-year-old on a skateboard, a yellow sheet tied round his shoulders.
Super Malul! It's you! I saw you! You have to take me. I'm fast, I'm quiet, I'm... not really quiet.
Dudi? I know you. You're the neighbour's kid.
Doesn't matter. I'm the sidekick. Come on, an old lady is stuck at the crossing by the synagogue.
cross: Super Malul?! I don't know you, but blue suits you.
Mrs Pnina, please, I'll carry the basket.
Basket? It's a bag. And it's the whole street's dinner. Three more crossings and I'm done.
I'll mark the way with the sheet.
sidekick: Well? Am I helping or not? I even have a nickname: "The Sheet".
That nickname won't last a week.
rYes: Fine, you help. But I decide, and you don't run ahead.
Got it! ...Is a sheet safe near roads?
rSchool: Homework first. Heroes do it too.
And at the end a real cape. Not a sheet.
rLater: Oh. Okay. I'll wait. ...But I'm staying here.
cape: Super Malul, I won't let you down.
Dudi straightens up on the skateboard. The sheet flaps behind him. He falls in the end, but elegantly.

sm02_patrol.page: 📱 Rishon Without a Filter: a teen on a skateboard in a yellow sheet is escorting someone in blue. (940 likes. "He carried my bag" - Pnina, neighbour.)

sm03_fanclub.title: The Fan Club

obj.hide: Talk to Dudi by the fuel station before the fans arrive
obj.noa: Talk to the photographer standing to the side
obj.fans: Decide what to do about Orit's fan club

offer: The yellow fuel station. Orit holds a hand-painted sign: "Super Malul Fan Club. Wait at the till".
Super Malul! We have eight members, and three of them don't know you yet.
It's excellent. We have shirts too.
hide: Super Malul! Ten fans on one side and five on the other. I'm checking an escape route.
What escape route? We're here to help.
It's the other side of the station. There's a photographer there. I think she's following you.
noa: Excuse me, you're Super Malul, right? I'm Noa. I write for "Rishon Without a Filter".
I'm just trying to help people.
Everyone says that. Then it turns out they have something to hide. I'll look into it.
But don't worry. I don't publish before I'm sure. ...Usually.
fans: Well? What do you say to the fans? They've been standing there an hour.
rSelfie: One selfie. Then everyone goes home.
Did you hear that?! One selfie! A historic day.
Eight fans, three improvised capes, and one selfie taken far too many times.
rRules: Conditions: no chasing, no holding the cape, and no chairs from the butchers' house.
Accepted. I'll put it in the rules.
rRun: I'm running. Sorry, I'll be back.
He's running! It only makes them more curious!
Dudi runs after him, sheet and all. He's late, but he doesn't give up.
